mainTopic: Beitzah 37a: Why קידושין, חליצה and יבום count as רשות (optional acts), the reason they are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב (the worry of writing), and why הקדש, ערכין and חרמים are forbidden (they look like buying and selling).
overview: The amud finishes the משנה's list of acts the רבנן forbade on שבת and יום טוב. קידושין, חליצה and יבום count as רשות when the main מצוה is not being fulfilled: the man already has children, or there is an older brother. They are forbidden in case one writes a document. הקדש, ערכין and חרמים are forbidden because they look like מקח וממכר. Separating תרומות ומעשרות is forbidden even for a כהן who will eat them that day, but חלה from dough made on יום טוב may be separated. רבי יצחק explains that all three groups are שבות, listed from the obvious case to the surprising one. A משנה that allows lowering produce through a skylight on יום טוב seems to contradict our משנה's rule that the only difference from שבת is food preparation. אביי rejects רב יוסף's answer from רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, and רב פפא answers instead that our משנה follows בית שמאי and the skylight משנה follows בית הלל. A new משנה then teaches that animals, vessels and food follow the תחום of their owners, and the גמרא on it begins at the end of the עמוד.

steps.title: Betrothal is optional because he already has a wife and children
steps.stepSummary: This line ends the גמרא's answer about קידושין. It is called רשות because the case is a man who already has a wife and children.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It is needed for a case] where he already has a wife and children.
steps.whatsHappening: Our passage starts in the middle of an answer. The גמרא had asked why קידושין is called רשות when it seems to fulfill פריה ורביה. The answer: the case is a man who already has a wife and children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who already has a wife and children has already fulfilled פריה ורביה. So marrying another woman is an extra, optional act for him. That is why the משנה can place קידושין in the רשות group.

keyTerms.meaning: a wife and children
an optional act, not a required מצוה
the מצוה to have children
betrothing a woman (קידושין)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the end of a sentence that began earlier: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ אִשָּׁה וּבָנִים, meaning 'it is needed only where he already has a wife and children.'

phrases.english: where he already has a wife and children.
phrases.notes: The end of the answer to 'But isn't he doing a מצוה?' about betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer, begun earlier, to the question of why קידושין counts as רשות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Betrothing a woman is always the מצוה of פריה ורביה, so it should not be called רשות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a man who has already fulfilled פריה ורביה, so for him the betrothal is optional.

steps.title: Aren't חליצה and יבום real מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next items, חליצה and יבום, and asks how they can be called optional when they are מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'One may not do חליצה and one may not do יבום' [and listed these as optional acts]. But surely the person is doing a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first quotes the משנה's words about חליצה and יבום. Then it challenges the משנה for calling them רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה commands יבום or חליצה when a man dies without children. So it seems odd to list them in the 'optional' group instead of the מצוה group. The question attacks the משנה's own grouping.

keyTerms.meaning: performing חליצה, the ceremony that releases the widow from יבום
performing יבום, levirate marriage
but surely he is doing a מצוה!

phrases.english: One may not perform ḥalitza, nor perform levirate marriage.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: But surely he is performing a מצוה!
phrases.notes: The challenge: why are these called optional?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same challenge already raised against קידושין, now applied to the next items in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's placement of חליצה and יבום in the רשות group.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יבום and חליצה are commanded by the תורה, so they cannot be merely optional.

steps.title: When there is an older brother, the younger one's יבום is optional
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is discussing a case where an older brother exists. The main מצוה belongs to the oldest brother, so a younger brother's act counts as רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed only where there is an older brother, and the מצוה of יבום belongs first to the oldest brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. It is talking about a younger brother when an older brother is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The preferred way to do the מצוה is for the oldest brother to do יבום. If a younger brother steps in, he is not doing the main מצוה, so his act is classed as רשות. The act is still valid יבום. Only its ranking changes.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for [this specific case]
the older brother
the מצוה of יבום belongs first to the oldest brother

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a younger brother's יבום fails to work. It is fully valid יבום. It is only called רשות because he is not the preferred brother to perform it.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary only
phrases.notes: Introduces a narrowed case.

phrases.english: where there is an older brother,
and the מצוה is for the oldest to perform levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every act of יבום or חליצה is a full מצוה, so it belongs in the מצוה group.
steps.terutzMaskana: When an older brother exists, a younger brother's יבום or חליצה is valid but counts only as רשות.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'optional' group in the משנה (קידושין, חליצה, יבום) is explained by narrowing each case to a situation where the main מצוה is not being fulfilled: he already has children, or an older brother exists.

steps.title: What is the reason behind all these restrictions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why all the acts in this group are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for all of these, what is the reason [they are forbidden]?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא asks for the single reason behind the whole רשות group, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these acts, such as judging, betrothing, חליצה or יבום, is a forbidden labor on its own. So the גמרא needs to explain why the רבנן forbade them.

keyTerms.meaning: and all of them
what is the reason?

phrases.english: And in all these cases, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the cases to explaining why they are forbidden.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason the רשות acts are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: A decree in case one writes a document
steps.stepSummary: All these acts are forbidden by a גזירה, because a person might write a document, which is forbidden מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a rabbinic decree, in case he writes [a document].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. The רבנן forbade these acts because people usually write a document for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court ruling, a betrothal, חליצה and יבום usually come with written records, such as a verdict, a שטר קידושין, a שטר חליצה or a כתובה. Writing is a real מלאכה. To keep people away from it, the רבנן banned the acts themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: a protective rabbinic decree
in case he writes

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of a גזירה. The act itself is permitted, but it is banned to prevent a real מלאכה (writing) that often goes along with it.

phrases.english: It is a decree lest one write.
phrases.notes: For example, a verdict, a betrothal document, a ḥalitza document, or a marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: These acts are forbidden by a גזירה, out of concern that a person will write a document, which is a forbidden מלאכה.

steps.title: Consecrating, valuations and חרמים are forbidden because they look like commerce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's מצוה group (הקדש, ערכין, חרמים) and explains that they are forbidden because they resemble buying and selling.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'And these are [forbidden even though they are] for a מצוה: one may not consecrate, one may not make a valuation vow, and one may not declare a חרם.' The reason is a decree because they look like buying and selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next group in the משנה, the acts done as a מצוה. It quotes them and gives the reason they are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these acts transfers ownership of property to the בית המקדש or to the כהנים. Transferring ownership looks like a business deal, and מקח וממכר is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב. So the רבנן forbade these acts too, even though they are מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: consecrating property to the בית המקדש
making a valuation vow (ערכין)
declaring property חרם, dedicated to the כהנים or the בית המקדש
buying and selling, commerce

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the reason here is different from step 5. The רשות group is banned because of writing. This מצוה group is banned because it looks like commerce.
steps.whatToRemember: Two groups, two reasons: the רשות acts are forbidden in case one writes a document, and the מצוה acts of הקדש, ערכין and חרמים are forbidden because they look like מקח וממכר.

phrases.english: And these are the ones notable because of a מצוה:
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: one may not consecrate, nor take a valuation vow,
nor declare property dedicated (ḥerem).
It is a decree due to commerce.
phrases.notes: The גמרא's explanation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next category in the משנה and gives a different reason for its ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדש, ערכין and חרמים are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב by a גזירה, because transferring property resembles מקח וממכר.

steps.title: Why say that separating תרומה is forbidden? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that one may not separate תרומות ומעשרות on יום טוב and asks why this needs saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may not separate תרומות and מעשרות.' The גמרא asks: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה. It then challenges it, saying the line seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating תרומות ומעשרות turns forbidden טבל into food that may be eaten. That counts as 'fixing' something, which is clearly forbidden on יום טוב. So why would the משנה bother to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: Separate (literally 'lift up') the required portions from produce
The portions that must be separated from produce and given to a כהן or a לוי
'It is obvious!' A challenge that asks why something needed to be said

phrases.english: And one may not separate (lit. lift up)
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: terumot and tithes.
That is obvious!
phrases.notes: Separating makes טבל usable, which is like fixing an item

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line 'ולא מגביהין תרומות ומעשרות'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separating these portions is clearly a forbidden act of fixing, so the line seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Forbidden even if the כהן gets it today
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the משנה forbids separating even when the תרומה would be given to a כהן that same day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: The line was needed only to teach that it is forbidden even in order to give it to a כהן on that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge. The משנה teaches something that is not obvious: even when the כהן could eat the תרומה today, separating it is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought it would be allowed. The כהן could eat the תרומה on יום טוב, so separating it might look like normal food preparation. The משנה teaches that it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (a teaching quoted from a תנאי source)
'It was needed only for...' The formula that shows the new point of a ruling
On that same day

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
It was needed only
to give it to a priest on that same day.
phrases.notes: Even then it is forbidden

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a non-obvious case that the line comes to teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separating for a כהן who will eat it today might be allowed as food preparation.

steps.title: Exception: dough that needs חלה on יום טוב itself
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition applies only to produce that was already טבל before יום טוב. Dough that first becomes obligated in חלה on יום טוב may have its חלה separated and given to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to produce that was already טבל from yesterday. But produce that became טבל today, such as dough from which we must separate חלה, we separate and give to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the rule it just taught. It applies only to food that already needed separating before יום טוב. Dough made on יום טוב is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce that was טבל yesterday could have been fixed before יום טוב, so separating it now is not allowed. Dough only needs חלה once it is made on יום טוב, so separating חלה is part of that day's permitted food preparation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And these words apply only...' A phrase that introduces a limit on a rule
Became טבל, meaning produce that is forbidden to eat until its portions are separated
From yesterday (before יום טוב)
Dough
The portion separated from dough and given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Separating from produce that was טבל before יום טוב is forbidden, even for a כהן today. חלה from dough made on יום טוב may be separated and given.

phrases.english: And these words apply only to
produce that was untithed since yesterday,
but produce that became untithed now (on יום טוב),
such as dough,
with regard to separating חלה from it,
we separate it and give it to a priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב יוסף's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibition covers only produce that was טבל before יום טוב. חלה from dough made on יום טוב may be separated and given to a כהן.

steps.title: Are the רשות and מצוה groups not שבות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's labels mean that only the first group is שבות, and that the רשות group and the מצוה group are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these acts: is there only the reason of רשות, and not the reason of שבות? And these acts: is there only the reason of מצוה, and not the reason of שבות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how the משנה is worded. The משנה calls only its first group 'שבות' and names the other groups 'רשות' and 'מצוה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That wording suggests the later groups are not forbidden because of שבות. But step 5 already said that all these acts are forbidden as a rabbinic גזירה, which is a שבות. So why do the labels change?

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic prohibition that keeps שבת and יום טוב as days of rest
An optional act, not a full מצוה
There is / there is not

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether these acts are forbidden. Everyone agrees they are. The question is why the משנה calls only the first group 'שבות'.

phrases.english: And these: is there only the reason of 'optional act',
and not the reason of שבות?
And these: is there only the reason of 'מצוה',
and not the reason of שבות?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי, מִשּׁוּם רְשׁוּת אִיכָּא, מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the structure of the משנה's three groups
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's labels 'משום רשות' and 'משום מצוה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The labels suggest these acts are not שבות. But they are forbidden only as rabbinic שבות.

steps.title: The משנה builds up: 'not only this, but even that'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that all three groups are שבות. The משנה lists them in rising order: plain שבות, then שבות of a רשות act, then שבות of a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The משנה speaks in the style of 'there is no need to say.' There is no need to say that plain שבות is forbidden; even שבות of a רשות act is also forbidden. And there is no need to say that שבות of a רשות act is forbidden; even שבות of a מצוה is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question. All the groups are שבות. The משנה's labels just show that each new group is a bigger surprise than the one before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain שבות, with no מצוה at all, is clearly forbidden. A רשות act has some value, yet it is still forbidden. A full מצוה is the hardest case, yet it is forbidden too. The words 'רשות' and 'מצוה' describe how strong each case is. They do not take away its שבות status.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He speaks in the style of no-need-to-say.' The list goes from the obvious case to the surprising one
Plain, alone, with nothing added
Even
Also

steps.whatToRemember: All three groups in the משנה are rabbinic שבות. The משנה lists them from least surprising to most surprising: plain, רשות, מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole structure of the משנה. It also shows a common pattern in the משנה: building from the obvious case to the surprising one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
He speaks in the style of 'there is no need to say':
There is no need to say that plain שבות is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ שְׁבוּת דִּרְשׁוּת נָמֵי אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but even שבות of an optional act is also forbidden.
And there is no need to say that שבות of an optional act is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ שְׁבוּת דְּמִצְוָה נָמֵי אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but even שבות of a מצוה is also forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא about the משנה's labels
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the משנה as a rising 'לא מבעיא' list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the first group is שבות. The others are forbidden for a different reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three groups are שבות. The labels show rising levels of surprise: plain, רשות, מצוה.

steps.title: Contradiction: lowering produce through a skylight
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה implies that every rabbinic prohibition applies on יום טוב just as on שבת. But another משנה permits lowering produce through a skylight on יום טוב and forbids it on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה said: 'All these were said about יום טוב,' meaning the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation. But another משנה teaches: 'We may lower produce through a skylight on יום טוב, but not on שבת!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of our משנה and then points to a different משנה that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is preparing food (אוכל נפש). Lowering produce through a skylight is not food preparation. It is hard work done only to save the produce from rain. Yet that משנה allows it on יום טוב and forbids it on שבת, so there seems to be a second difference after all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'All these were said about יום טוב.' The rabbinic prohibitions apply on יום טוב too.
'And they contrasted it.' This introduces a contradiction from another source.
We may lower or let down (produce)
A skylight, an opening in the roof
Food preparation, which is the one category of work allowed on יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: The full line of our משנה continues: 'there is no difference between יום טוב and שבת except food preparation.' The text here quotes only the opening words, but the contradiction is aimed at that whole rule.

phrases.english: All these they said [apply] on Yom Tov,
phrases.notes: Quoting our משנה. The implied continuation is that the only difference from שבת is food preparation.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One may lower [produce] through a skylight on Yom Tov,
phrases.notes: This is done to save the produce from rain.

phrases.english: but not on Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה after finishing the discussion of the three groups of שבות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule in our משנה that the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה shows a second difference: hard work done to prevent a loss, which is allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף: two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the two משניות follow different תנאים: one follows רבי אליעזר and the other follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not a problem. This משנה follows רבי אליעזר, and that משנה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the contradiction by saying each משנה reflects a different תנא's view. The next step brings his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה, which allows only food preparation, follows רבי אליעזר. He does not permit effort on יום טוב just to prevent a loss. The skylight משנה follows רבי יהושע, who does permit such effort. So the two משניות are not contradicting each other; they reflect a real disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult.' This opens an answer.
'This one ... that one.' Each source is assigned to a different view.
The תנא who is strict here
The תנא who is lenient here

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: This [follows] Rabbi Eliezer, that [follows] Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: Our משנה follows רבי אליעזר. The skylight משנה follows רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנאים (תנאי היא): each משנה follows a different opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות express one single view, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows רבי אליעזר (no effort just to prevent a loss). The skylight משנה follows רבי יהושע (effort to prevent a loss is allowed).

steps.title: The animals in the pit: רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's source is a ברייתא about a mother animal and its offspring (אותו ואת בנו) that fell into a pit on יום טוב. רבי אליעזר says to raise only the first, slaughter it, and feed the second where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: If a mother animal and its offspring fell into a pit on יום טוב, רבי אליעזר says: He raises the first one in order to slaughter it, and he slaughters it. For the second, he gives it food where it is, so that it will not die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree, starting with רבי אליעזר's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day, so only one of them can be eaten on יום טוב. Raising an animal from a pit is hard work, and רבי אליעזר allows it only for food. So the second animal must stay in the pit and be fed there. He does not allow the effort just to prevent its loss, which matches our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
A mother animal and its offspring, which may not be slaughtered on the same day
A pit
In order to slaughter it, meaning for the sake of food
Feeding it where it is, inside the pit

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְבוֹר —
phrases.english: As it was taught: A mother and its offspring that fell into a pit —
phrases.notes: This happened on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל מְנָת לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ וְשׁוֹחֲטוֹ,
phrases.english: He raises the first in order to slaughter it, and he slaughters it,
and for the second, he provides it food in its place
phrases.notes: He may not raise it, because it cannot be slaughtered today.

phrases.english: so that it will not die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רב יוסף's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רבי אליעזר does not allow effort on יום טוב just to prevent a loss
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about אותו ואת בנו that fell into a pit

steps.title: The animals in the pit: רבי יהושע's trick
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע allows raising the first animal 'to slaughter it,' then choosing not to, and then using a trick to raise the second as well. Afterwards he may slaughter whichever one he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: He raises the first in order to slaughter it, and then does not slaughter it. Then he uses a trick and raises the second. If he wants, he slaughters this one; if he wants, he slaughters that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהושע's lenient view, which completes רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a trick (הערמה), רבי יהושע lets both animals out of the pit, even though only one can be eaten. This shows that he allows effort on יום טוב to prevent a loss, here the loss of the animal that might die in the pit. That is the same reasoning behind lowering produce through a skylight, so the skylight משנה follows רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: And he does not slaughter it; he changes his mind
Uses a trick or pretext (הַעֲרָמָה)
If he wants, he slaughters this one. He may pick either animal.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר does not allow effort on יום טוב just to prevent a loss, and our משנה ('only food preparation') follows him. רבי יהושע does allow such effort, and the skylight משנה follows him. The contradiction is a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע does not openly permit raising an animal just to save it. He gets there through a trick: each animal is raised 'in order to slaughter it.' רב יוסף reads the willingness to allow this trick as proof that he cares about preventing loss.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל מְנָת לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ
phrases.english: He raises the first in order to slaughter it
and does not slaughter it,
and goes back, uses a trick, and raises the second.
phrases.notes: He claims he now prefers to slaughter the second one.

phrases.aramaic: רָצָה — זֶה שׁוֹחֵט, רָצָה — זֶה שׁוֹחֵט.
phrases.english: If he wishes, he slaughters this one; if he wishes, he slaughters that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the opposing view, which completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רבי יהושע allows effort on יום טוב to prevent a loss
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's ruling in the ברייתא allowing a trick to raise both animals

steps.title: אביי: Maybe רבי אליעזר Would Allow Moving the Produce
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף's proof. רבי אליעזר may have been strict with the animals only because the second animal could be fed in the pit. The produce on the roof has no such alternative, so he might allow saving it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How do you know? Perhaps רבי אליעזר was strict there only because the second animal could be fed where it is. But here, where feeding is not possible, he would not be strict!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions whether the ברייתא really proves what רב יוסף said. He suggests that רבי אליעזר's strictness might apply only to the animal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the animals, the owner loses nothing by leaving the second animal in the pit, because he can feed it there. With produce left out on the roof, there is no way to prevent the loss except by moving it. So רבי אליעזר's ruling does not prove he would forbid lowering the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
He only said his ruling up to this point (in this specific case)
Providing food or sustenance (here, feeding the animal in the pit)
There (the earlier case) and here (our case)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רבי אליעזר definitely permits moving the produce. He is only saying the proof is not airtight, since the two cases are different.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: From where [do you know this]?
phrases.notes: Addressed to רב יוסף

phrases.english: Perhaps he only said [his ruling]
Rabbi Eliezer, there [in the pit case],
because it is possible [to save it] by feeding it,
phrases.notes: The second animal can be fed in the pit

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר בְּפַרְנָסָה — לָא!
phrases.english: but here, where feeding is not possible, he would not [forbid it]!
phrases.notes: The produce on the roof

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof that רב יוסף brought from רבי אליעזר's ruling in the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי אליעזר, not his ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pit case has an alternative (feeding the animal) that the produce case lacks, so the two cases cannot be compared

steps.title: אביי: Maybe רבי יהושע Would Forbid Moving the Produce
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers a second rejection from the other side. רבי יהושע may have been lenient only because a trick was available to raise the second animal. With the produce, no trick is possible, so he might forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: Perhaps רבי יהושע was lenient there only because it was possible to use a trick. But here, where a trick is not possible, he would not be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now attacks the proof from רבי יהושע's side. His leniency may also be limited to the animal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע allowed raising the second animal only through a trick, where the owner acts as if he plans to slaughter it. Lowering produce through a skylight is plainly an act of saving property, so no trick is available. That means רבי יהושע might be strict here, and רב יוסף's proof falls apart from both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or else
To use a trick or clever strategy

steps.whatToRemember: אביי shows that neither רבי אליעזר nor רבי יהושע clearly matches the produce case. So רב יוסף's answer, that each משנה follows a different תנא, has no solid source.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר
phrases.english: Alternatively: he only said [his ruling]
Rabbi Yehoshua, there [in the pit case],
because it is possible to use a trick.
phrases.notes: Pretending to raise each animal in order to slaughter it

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר לְאַעֲרוֹמֵי — לָא.
phrases.english: But here, where a trick is not possible, he would not [permit it].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel rejection, this time aimed at the רבי יהושע half of רב יוסף's proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי יהושע and so completes the rejection of רב יוסף's answer
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהושע's leniency depends on a trick that cannot be used with the produce

steps.title: רב פפא: The Two משניות Follow בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא drops רב יוסף's approach. He answers the contradiction differently: one משנה follows בית שמאי and the other follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: There is no difficulty. This משנה follows בית שמאי, and that משנה follows בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי knocked down רב יוסף's answer, רב פפא gives a new answer to the contradiction from Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats יום טוב the same as שבת, and that matches בית שמאי. The skylight משנה is more lenient on יום טוב, and that matches בית הלל. The two משניות still follow different opinions, but now the disagreement is between בית שמאי and בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the previous answer and offer a new one)
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
The school of שמאי (usually the stricter view)
The school of הלל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which is which. Our strict משנה (יום טוב is like שבת) follows בית שמאי. The lenient skylight משנה follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
phrases.notes: The word אלא signals that רב יוסף's answer is dropped

phrases.english: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, הָא בֵּית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: This [follows] Beit Shammai, that [follows] Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, הָא בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected answer with a new one to the same contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two sources to different opinions (בית שמאי and בית הלל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות contradict each other about whether rabbinic prohibitions apply equally on יום טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows בית שמאי (יום טוב is as strict as שבת). The skylight משנה follows בית הלל (יום טוב is more lenient).

steps.title: Source: Carrying a Child, לולב, or ספר תורה on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's source is a משנה. בית שמאי forbid carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the רשות הרבים on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say: We may not carry out a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the רשות הרבים. And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about how strict יום טוב is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these items is food, and carrying them out is forbidden on שבת. בית שמאי treat יום טוב the same way, which matches our משנה. בית הלל allow it on יום טוב, which shows they make יום טוב more lenient than שבת, matching the skylight משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
We may not carry out
The public domain
They permit

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: בית שמאי say יום טוב is as strict as שבת except for food preparation, and that is our משנה. בית הלל are more lenient on יום טוב, and that is the skylight משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Practical הלכה usually follows בית הלל, so it matters that the more lenient view of יום טוב belongs to them.

phrases.english: As we learned [in a Mishnah]: Beit Shammai say:
We may not carry out a small child,
phrases.notes: A child who cannot walk on his own

phrases.english: nor a lulav,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: nor a Torah scroll into the public domain,
phrases.notes: On יום טוב

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel permit [it].

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין לֹא אֶת הַקָּטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רב פפא's answer
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי treat יום טוב as strictly as שבת, while בית הלל are more lenient on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the רשות הרבים on יום טוב

steps.title: Maybe בית שמאי only forbade carrying out, not moving things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that בית שמאי's strictness may apply only to הוצאה (carrying into the public domain), not to טלטול (moving objects). If so, רב פפא's proof would fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that is not so. בית שמאי only said their ruling there about carrying out to the public domain. But about moving things around, they did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא's proof. It suggests that the source he quoted is about a different kind of action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's source was about carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the רשות הרבים, which is הוצאה. The produce case is only about moving produce down from a roof, which is טלטול. If בית שמאי are strict only about הוצאה, they might allow lowering the produce on יום טוב. Then they too would hold a second difference between יום טוב and שבת, and our משנה ('only food preparation') could not be attributed to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps that is not so (a formula that questions a proof)
They only said their ruling up to this point
Carrying an object from one domain to another
Moving an object from place to place, without carrying it out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up הוצאה and טלטול. הוצאה means carrying from one domain into another, such as from a house to the street. טלטול means just moving something around, even inside one domain.

phrases.english: Perhaps that is not so,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai only stated their view there
about carrying out to the public domain,
phrases.notes: The case of the child, לולב, and ספר תורה

phrases.english: but about moving objects, not.
phrases.notes: For example, lowering the produce from the roof

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא לָא הִיא, עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof that רב פפא brought in Step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the הוצאה משנה. It does not reject רב פפא's basic answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source is about הוצאה, but the produce case is only about טלטול. The two may not be comparable.

steps.title: The limits on moving things exist because of carrying out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The rule against needless טלטול was made because of the concern about הוצאה, so the two go together. רב פפא's proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that moving things is not for the sake of carrying out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 20 with a rhetorical question. This saves רב פפא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים limited moving things that are not needed for יום טוב because of a worry that a person might end up carrying them out to the public domain. So if בית שמאי were strict about הוצאה, they would also be strict about טלטול and would forbid lowering the produce on יום טוב. This means our משנה (no difference except food preparation) can follow בית שמאי, and the lenient skylight משנה follows בית הלל, as רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a rhetorical question introducing a refutation)
For the sake of carrying out; here, a rule made because of the concern about הוצאה

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's answer stands. One משנה follows בית שמאי and the other follows בית הלל. The limit on טלטול is a fence around הוצאה, so being strict on one means being strict on the other.

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ טִלְטוּל לָאו צוֹרֶךְ הוֹצָאָה הוּא?
phrases.english: Is that to say that moving is not for the sake of carrying out?
phrases.notes: Meaning: the ban on needless moving was made because of carrying out

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ טִלְטוּל לָאו צוֹרֶךְ הוֹצָאָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 20 and brings back רב פפא's proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole distinction between הוצאה and טלטול made in Step 20
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The limit on טלטול was made because of הוצאה, so the two cannot be separated.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא's answer holds: the two משניות follow בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.title: Animals and vessels share their owner's travel limit
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that animals and vessels have the same תחום as their owner. This stays true even if the owner gave the animal to his son or to a shepherd.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal and vessels are like the feet of the owner. If someone gives his animal to his son or to a shepherd, they are still like the feet of the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that on יום טוב, an animal or vessel may only go as far as its owner may go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every person has a תחום, a limited distance he may walk on יום טוב. An owner's property is tied to his תחום. The person who is only caring for the animal, such as a son or shepherd, does not change this, because ownership is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the start of a new משנה)
Like the feet of the owner: it shares his travel limit
One who hands over
Shepherd

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'like the feet of the owner' means sharing the owner's תחום, his limit on how far he may travel. It is not about who is holding or guarding the animal.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An animal and vessels are as the feet of the owner.
One who hands over his animal to his son or to a shepherd,
these are as the feet of the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that opens a new topic, the תחום of property
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal or vessel follows its owner's תחום on יום טוב, even when someone else is caring for it.

steps.title: Vessels belonging to brothers in one house
steps.stepSummary: If a vessel is set aside for one brother, it follows that brother's תחום. If it is shared, it may only go where all of the brothers may go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Vessels set aside for one of the brothers in the house are like his feet. Vessels that are not set aside for one brother are limited to the place where all the brothers may go.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the case of brothers who own vessels together, for example vessels they inherited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel used only by one brother counts as his, so it follows his תחום alone. A shared vessel belongs to all of them, so it is limited by each brother's תחום. This matters if one brother made an עירוב תחומין and the others did not. A shared vessel may then go only where every brother is allowed to go.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside for one person's use
Brothers
Limited to the place where all of them may go

phrases.aramaic: כֵּלִים הַמְיוּחָדִין לְאֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין שֶׁבַּבַּיִת —
phrases.english: Vessels set aside for one of the brothers in the house,
these are as his feet.
And those that are not set aside for one brother,
these are as the place where they all may go.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּלִים הַמְיוּחָדִין לְאֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין שֶׁבַּבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of 'like the feet of the owner' to property with more than one owner
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel set aside for one brother follows his תחום. A shared vessel is limited by the תחום of every brother.

steps.title: A borrowed vessel depends on when it was borrowed
steps.stepSummary: A vessel borrowed before יום טוב follows the borrower's תחום. A vessel borrowed on יום טוב itself follows the lender's תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone borrows a vessel from his friend on ערב יום טוב, it is like the feet of the borrower. If he borrows it on יום טוב, it is like the feet of the lender.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows that timing matters. What counts is who had the vessel at the moment יום טוב began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel's תחום is fixed when יום טוב starts. If the borrower already had it then, it is set as his. If the owner still had it then, it stays tied to the owner's תחום even after it is lent out.

keyTerms.meaning: The borrower
The lender
The day before יום טוב

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מֵחֲבֵירוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: One who borrows a vessel from his friend on the eve of the Festival,
it is as the feet of the borrower.
If he borrowed it on the Festival, it is as the feet of the lender.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מֵחֲבֵירוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a timing rule to the idea of 'like the feet of the owner'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel's תחום is set by whoever had it when יום טוב began.

steps.title: Borrowed ingredients in a dough, and רבי יהודה on water
steps.stepSummary: A dough made with borrowed spices, water, or salt follows the תחום of both women. רבי יהודה says borrowed water does not count, because it has no real substance in the dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, if a woman borrowed spices, water, or salt from her friend for her dough, the food is like the feet of both of them. רבי יהודה exempts the case of water, because water has no real substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case of mixed ownership. A borrowed ingredient goes into a food, and then רבי יהודה disagrees about water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrowed ingredient keeps its link to its owner's תחום. So the finished food may only go where both women may go. רבי יהודה holds that water gets absorbed into the dough and leaves nothing you can point to, so it does not tie the dough to its first owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Spices
Dough
Like the feet of both of them: limited by both women's תחום
Exempts; here, says the limit does not apply
Real, noticeable substance

steps.whatToRemember: The main rule of this משנה: property follows its owner's תחום, and the תחום is set when יום טוב begins. When more than one person owns something, it is limited by everyone's תחום. רבי יהודה holds that something with no real substance, like water in a dough, does not create such a link.

phrases.english: And similarly, a woman who borrowed from her friend
spices, or water and salt for her dough,
these are as the feet of both of them.
Rabbi Yehuda exempts in the case of water,
because it has no real substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the borrowing rule to ingredients mixed into food, and adds רבי יהודה's dissent
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food made with a borrowed ingredient follows both owners' תחום. רבי יהודה excludes water, which has no real substance.

steps.title: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא section begins. It names the משנה it is about to comment on, but the comment itself comes on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The משנה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to talk about the משנה we just learned about the תחום of animals and vessels. This line only sets up the next move. The actual statement about the משנה comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marker גמ׳ shows that we are moving from the משנה text to the גמרא's discussion. The word מתניתין points back to the rulings in Steps 22-25. In the following words, the גמרא will say whose opinion this משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא. It marks where the Talmud's discussion of the משנה begins.
"Our משנה". The משנה we just learned.
The distance limit around a person's location on שבת or יום טוב. The משנה is about whose limit items follow.

steps.confusionAlert: This passage is not a full statement. 'מתניתין' is only the subject of a sentence that continues on the next עמוד, so do not look for a ruling here yet.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Our Mishnah
phrases.notes: Opening marker of the גמרא section. The sentence about the משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's rulings in Steps 22-25 to the start of the גמרא's analysis of that משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line opens the גמרא's statement about which opinion the משנה follows.
